Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Time: 10:00 AM PST / 18:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); David Morales (Skyline Proc); Priya Shah (Skyline Legal); Ethan Park (Skyline CTO); Sofia Ramos (Skyline Sec)
Meeting ID: fireflies-20260321-83421
Links referenced: Redwood MSA v4 (link), Standard SLA appendix (link), SOC2 report (placeholder link)

Summary:
Quick procurement/legal run-through of MSA/DPA and SLAs, high-level security artifacts request, pricing ask for 4-week Dedicated trial, and next steps to align redlines. Customer emphasized data residency and strict audit trail for energy operations data.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA encryption/data localization
- SLA targets and remedies (uptime, latency tiers for Dedicated)
- Pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity trial and bumping to production
- Onboarding timeline, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs

Action items (brief): Jordan to send redlines; Maya to send certs; schedule bench; Priya will review DPA clauses.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, with Maya our SE.
[00:10] David Morales: Yeah thanks Jordan, we have, uh, most of the procurement and legal folks here. So we wanna run through the MSA and the DPA and make sure the SLAs line up with our requirements.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya here, I'm the legal counsel. Our main ask is we need clear data residency, encryption at rest and in transit, and audit logs retained for five years — that was the vendor requirement from our compliance team.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Got it, Priya. Quick note, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments, and we can provide KMS/HSM integration docs — I'll share those.
[00:45] Ethan Park: Hi, Ethan. From an infra perspective we also want to know about private VPC deployment options, and whether the control plane can be kept on-prem or in their VPC.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: Short answer — for Private we provide a customer-controlled control plane option, yes. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and VPC-only egress. There's an on-prem package too if you need air-gapped.
[01:20] Sofia Ramos: Sorry quick interjection, what about audit logs? Will Redwood keep immutable logs and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[01:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we have configurable export to S3 and can forward to Splunk/Datadog; logs include token-level traces and model call metadata. Retention policy is configurable per contract — default is 90 days but we can extend.
[01:45] Priya Shah: The compliance team wants five years and legal will need indemnities around data breaches plus subprocessor disclosures in the DPA.
[01:55] Jordan Lee: Understood. On indemnity — we have standard language, but we can escalate exceptions with legal ops. We'll mark that for the MSA redline convo.
[02:10] David Morales: Pricing — we need a committed cost for a 4-week Dedicated pilot. We're trying to justify this internally as a pilot ahead of a Q3 roll-out.
[02:20] Jordan Lee: We can put together a dedicated pricing proposal: reserved capacity for the pilot, plus a burst buffer if needed. We'll include estimated token throughput and cost per-token delta vs hosted.
[02:35] Ethan Park: Also, latency SLOs — for our control systems the 99th percentile needs to be under 250ms for short prompts. Can your Dedicated offering guarantee that?
[02:48] Maya Chen: We publish performance profiles. Dedicated on provisioned A100-equivalent pools typically hit low-200ms p99 for sub-256 token requests, but it depends on model and quantization. We can run a benchmark using your prompt set to validate.
[03:10] Priya Shah: SLA remedies? Do you do service credits only or also termination rights after repeated failures?
[03:20] Jordan Lee: Standard is service credits; termination for repeated and material breaches can be discussed as part of enterprise terms. We'll surface the SLA appendix which includes uptime, latency tiers, and remedies.
[03:35] David Morales: Ok we also need to confirm data residency — our data must remain in the us-west region. Does Redwood support geo-fenced deployments?
[03:45] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pin workloads to regions and we can run Dedicated capacity in a specific region. For Private installs, it's obviously fully within your network.
[03:55] Sofia Ramos: Encryption at rest — we need BYOK with rotation policies.
[04:00] Maya Chen: BYOK supported via KMS integrations; we support scheduled rotation and key scoping. I'll send KMS doc with examples.
[04:15] Priya Shah: For the DPA, we need subprocessors list and 30 days notice for changes. Also, deletion requests — we need the ability to request deletion and a certificate of deletion.
[04:28] Jordan Lee: Subprocessors list is current in the vendor portal; we'll share the latest. Deletion certificates can be provided — we'll confirm the process.
[04:40] David Morales: On onboarding, what's the timeline and who will own the technical onboarding from Redwood?
[04:48] Jordan Lee: Maya will lead the technical onboarding; typical timeline for a Dedicated pilot is 2-3 weeks for provision and config, plus any legal/contract cycle time.
[05:00] Ethan Park: For benchmarks — we'll provide a sample prompt set and test corpus, can you run in our VPC or do you need staging infra?
[05:10] Maya Chen: We can run a benchmark inside your VPC for Private, or we can simulate Dedicated traffic in our staging infra. For final numbers, running within your network (VPC peered) is best.
[05:25] Priya Shah: A few specific redline items — limitation of liability cap needs to be discussed, we prefer per-incident carveouts for security incidents.
[05:35] Jordan Lee: Noted, we'll flag those to legal ops.
[05:40] David Morales: Any competitors we should be concerned about? Our infra team evaluated Anthropic and some internal cloud-based solutions.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: Right, Anthropic was mentioned; we discussed differentiators around Dedicated cost controls and unified tooling.
[05:55] Priya Shah: Also want clarity on export control and whether models or weights are considered PII or regulated — any comment?
[06:05] Maya Chen: Models/weights are not PII but platform handles customer data per DPA; for regulated content we recommend Private or Dedicated with KMS.
[06:18] David Morales: Ok, next steps — send redlines and security artifacts.
[06:22] Jordan Lee: We'll do that. Maya, you'll send the certs?
[06:25] Maya Chen: Yep, SOC2, ISO27001, pen test summary, KMS integration doc — I'll share in the next two days.
[06:33] Priya Shah: We'll aim to return initial redlines within a week of receiving docs.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: Great. Anything else?
[06:42] Sofia Ramos: One last question — do you support SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[06:47] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning both supported; we'll add implementation notes.
[06:55] David Morales: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll expect the paperwork and the benchmark schedule.
[07:00] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the items discussed.

End of transcript.
